chunks: If you want, I will, as a second example, relate to you concerning Mūsā, the Interlocutor of Allāh (a.s.) when he said:
“O Allāh! I need whatever good Thou mayest grant me.” (Qur’ān, 28:24)

By Allāh, he asked Him only for bread to eat because he was used to eating the herbs of the earth, and the greenness of the herbs could be seen from the delicate skin of his belly due to his thinness and paucity of his flesh.

key_terms.كَلِيمِ اللَّهِ: The Interlocutor of God (a title for Prophet Moses)

ai.seo_question: What was the nature of Prophet Moses' diet and his specific request for 'good' in the Quran?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi uses this verse to illustrate the profound asceticism (zuhd) of Prophet Moses, clarifying that his plea for 'good' (khayr) referred to basic sustenance rather than luxury, as he subsisted on simple herbs. This interpretation underscores the Shia emphasis on spiritual poverty and humility, contrasting divine favor with material simplicity, and serves as a model for believers to emulate in their own spiritual journeys.
